answer: Each identity claims one trellis cell, mounts one crystal, posts an 80-credit bond, and files a key-signed diffraction log. A sparrow observer photographs it and files the image. An auditor recomputes spacing from the log and matches it to the sparrow image and cell tag; a mismatch or reused fingerprint burns the bond. First cell 35 credits, kth 35+5(k-1), 1000th 5030; 1000 fakes pay 2,532,500 fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-crystal ring fails: one fingerprint cannot match two cells, so both bonds burn. An honest operator claims one cell, pays 35 once, and recovers the 80 bond after audit.
